content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with a cookie filling consists of bite‑size sweets coated in milk or dark chocolate and filled with a soft, crumbly cookie mixture. They offer a sweet, creamy chocolate flavor combined with a tender, slightly crunchy cookie interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipe for chocolate candy with a cookie filling appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
The filling typically contains butter, sugar, vanilla and finely crushed cookie pieces.
These candies are popular as holiday gifts, especially for New Year’s and Valentine’s Day.
In different countries the filling may be enriched with nuts, caramel or fruit bits.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate, especially dark, provides flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Contains simple carbohydrates that can quickly replenish energy stores.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium present in cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: The candies contain milk chocolate, which can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: A large amount of sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of caffeine, which should be considered for children and caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies as a standalone snack, add them to dessert assortments, or use them as decorative elements in baked goods. Keep them dry to prevent the chocolate from melting.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent chocolate bloom.
